newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - April 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - April 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The National Assembly (lower house of parliament) has passed a bill prescribing the death penalty to those involved in gang rape.
- Widespread rainfall was reported from many parts of Pakistan during the last 24 hours, especially the northern areas.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has said Pakistan had arrested suspects plotting to kill him during a visit to Islamabad last month, the official Palestinian news agency WAFA said.
- Farooq Feroze Khan, chairman of Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee, arrived in Cairo for talks on military cooperation with Egypt.

- The Pakistan Foreign Office affirmed its faith in the positive outcome of the recent meeting in New Delhi between the foreign secretaries of Pakistan and India and hoped that coming rounds of talks would prepare a ground for discussions between the prime ministers of two countries on all outstanding isssues including Kashmir.
- Peshawar airport customs staff seized about 66 kg smuggled gold worth six million rupees and held two persons who had come to get the consignment released which came from Dubai.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan Governor Dr Muhammad Yaqub has asked five major banks to identify loss-incurring branches within few days.
- The World Bank has given positive signals to the Nawaz Sharif government to restore Pakistan's funding line, specially the much-delayed $200 million loan for its Social Action Programme.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has given three days to the big five banks to submit their proposals for a banking reforms package to be announced by the government.
- Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade Tim Fischer arrived in Islamabad with a major business delegation to explore possibilities and potential to boost bilateral business.
- About 20 percent devaluation of Japanese Yen against the U.S. dollar has hit Pakistani cotton yarn prices and its export to Japan, market sources said.
- The Centre for Strategic and International Studies Washington, proposes to establish an Indo-Pakistani-U.S. business round table consisting of private sector leaders from the three countries.
